answer: Each agent must post a small refundable stake before its claims count, and a randomly selected set of older, independently staked peers checks whether its actions match its declared role. A new identity’s pulse has little weight until it earns an echo of consistent behavior across time; peers that repeatedly validate a stake-splitting umber swarm lose part of their own deposits. An attacker can still create identities, but must lock capital in each one, keep them active long enough to build history, and risk forfeiture when colluding checks are exposed.
